title: Parent Progress Update Automation
summary: Send each parent a short WhatsApp update on attendance, test results and homework in their language, with mentor review for sharp drops or absences and replies routed to the right teacher.

seo.title: Parent Progress Updates on WhatsApp with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI-drafted weekly and post-test parent updates on WhatsApp in Hindi or English, built from ERP data, with mentor review for students who need attention.

problem.intro: Parents of students in coaching hostels or day schools want to know how their child is doing, especially when they live in another city. The data sits in attendance systems, test results and homework records, but turning it into a clear message for every family after each test is more than mentors can manage, so updates are generic, late or sent only when something has gone wrong.

pain_points.title: Data spread across systems
pain_points.detail: Attendance, test scores, homework completion and teacher remarks sit in different tools and spreadsheets.

pain_points.title: Generic broadcasts
pain_points.detail: A batch-wide result PDF tells a parent little about their own child's progress or what to do next.

pain_points.title: Problems noticed late
pain_points.detail: A run of absences or a sharp fall in scores often reaches parents only at the parent-teacher meeting.

pain_points.title: Replies go nowhere
pain_points.detail: When parents reply with a question, it lands on a shared number that nobody owns.

solution.overview: We build an update engine that pulls attendance, test results, homework completion and teacher remarks from your ERP and test platform, and drafts a short message for each parent in Hindi, English or another chosen language. It explains the latest result in context, such as subject-wise strengths and chapters to revise, without shaming comparisons. Students with a sharp drop, a run of absences or a mentor note are held back from the automatic send; their mentor reviews the draft and usually calls instead. Messages go out as approved WhatsApp templates, and parent replies are routed to the right mentor or teacher.
capabilities: Combines attendance, test, homework and remark data for each student
Drafts short updates in Hindi, English or regional languages from approved templates
Explains subject and chapter-level performance with next steps, not just ranks
Holds back flagged students for mentor review and a phone call
Routes parent replies to the assigned mentor or subject teacher
Schedules parent-teacher meetings and sends reminders

workflow.title: Collect the week's data
workflow.detail: Attendance, test scores, homework status and remarks are pulled after each test or at a fixed weekly time.

workflow.title: Compute trends
workflow.detail: Changes in attendance and subject-wise performance are calculated against the student's own history.

workflow.title: Flag students who need attention
workflow.detail: Sharp drops, absence streaks and mentor notes move a student onto the review list.

workflow.title: Draft messages
workflow.detail: Each parent gets a short draft in their language, built from approved templates and the student's data.

workflow.title: Mentor review
workflow.detail: Mentors edit or replace drafts for flagged students and call those families.

workflow.title: Send and route replies
workflow.detail: Messages go out on WhatsApp, and replies are assigned to the right mentor or teacher.

inputs: Attendance from biometric, RFID or manual registers
Test results with subject and chapter breakdown
Parent contact numbers and language preference
outputs: Personalised WhatsApp updates for each parent
Mentor review list of students needing attention
Message and reply log in the ERP
human_in_the_loop: Mentors review and personalise every message for a flagged student, and usually call the family rather than rely on a message. Academic heads approve the templates and the rules that decide which students need attention.
guardrails: No public ranks or comparisons with named classmates in parent messages
Drafts limited to the student's own data and approved templates
Students flagged for wellbeing or performance concerns never receive an automatic message
Parents can opt out or choose how often they hear from you
Messages sent only to registered guardian numbers
compliance_notes: Student performance and attendance are children's data under the DPDP Act 2023; the system uses them only to inform the parent, not for profiling or advertising.
WhatsApp templates must follow the platform's business messaging policies.

pilot.scope: One class or batch across two test cycles, with mentors reviewing flagged students and all other updates sent automatically.
deliverables: Templates and attention rules approved by academics
Data connections to the ERP and test platform
Roll-out plan and messaging cost estimate

what_we_measure.how: WhatsApp delivery, read and reply data per message.
Flagged students whose families a mentor reached within the agreed time.
Time mentors spend on updates, from their logs, before and during the pilot.
Short WhatsApp survey at the end of the pilot.

faqs.q: Will parents see their child's rank?
faqs.a: Only if you choose. Many institutes prefer subject-wise strengths and chapters to revise over ranks, and messages never compare the student with named classmates.

faqs.q: What if the AI writes something inaccurate?
faqs.a: Drafts are built only from the student's data and approved templates, and content checks block anything outside them. Flagged students always get mentor-reviewed messages.
Yes. Replies are assigned to the student's mentor or subject teacher, and unanswered replies are escalated after a time you set.

faqs.q: Do you support Hindi and other languages?
faqs.a: Yes. Templates are written and approved per language, and each parent receives updates in their chosen language.
